Injury status introduces stochastic variables that alter baseline performance expectations. The interplay between these elements creates a dynamic risk landscape. The dual nature of the spread (consensus vs. divergent sharp money) implies a potential mispricing opportunity. The injury report adds uncertainty to the baseline model, affecting both offensive and defensive projections. These factors combine to generate a multi-dimensional state space for game prediction. The failure mode occurs when sharp money does not reflect true skill differentials, leading to overconfidence in consensus lines. Conversely, ignoring injury impacts can result in underestimating volatility. The system requires continuous updating based on new data streams.
